nodes.label: README - Point of Sale Water Station
Offline-First Sync Architecture
nodes.rationale: The shop PC must work with no internet at all: every admin write lands in local SQLite first and is pushed to TiDB when connectivity returns, so a dropped connection never blocks a sale.

nodes.label: Outbox Write Queue (data/outbox.jsonl)
nodes.rationale: Appending one JSON line per write keeps the durable queue independent of SQLite transactions and lets the 15-second sync service replay anything unsent.

nodes.label: Customer-Side Offline Order Retry Queue
nodes.rationale: A failed website submission is stored on the customer's device and retried; the client-generated order id makes the retry idempotent so no duplicate orders appear.

nodes.label: Append-Only Stock Ledger (inventory_logs)
nodes.rationale: On-hand is derived as SUM(change_qty) over additive rows instead of a mutable counter, so two offline devices cannot overwrite each other and stock cannot drift.

nodes.label: Track Stock Toggle and Refill-as-Service Rule
nodes.rationale: A refill is a service (the customer brings the container), so counting it is meaningless; the Refill category name pre-flips the switch off while keeping it overridable.

nodes.label: Immutable Price History Rule
nodes.rationale: Each order line stores the name, unit and price it was sold at, so changing a product price affects future orders only and historical orders stay valid financial records; recalcOrder sums the stored line_total_cents, guarded by npm run test:history.

nodes.label: Integer Centavos Money Rule
nodes.rationale: Money is stored as integer centavos in *_cents columns, never floats, to avoid rounding drift when totals are summed on both the local admin and the cloud.

nodes.label: Client-Generated ULID Primary Keys
nodes.rationale: Clients must be able to create rows while offline without asking a server for an id; ULIDs are also sortable and make retried submissions idempotent.

nodes.label: Last-Write-Wins Conflict Resolution
nodes.rationale: Mutable rows carry updated_at (epoch ms) and resolve conflicts by newest timestamp, which is enough for a single-shop deployment syncing against TiDB.

nodes.label: Soft Deletes via deleted_at
nodes.rationale: Rows are never physically removed so a delete on one device propagates as a timestamped tombstone instead of being resurrected by the next pull.

nodes.label: Order Discounts Engine
nodes.rationale: Discounts apply to goods only, never the delivery fee, and are clamped to the subtotal so a total can never go negative; stored as discount_cents, discount_percent and discount_reason, admin-only.

nodes.label: Automatic SQLite Backup Snapshots
nodes.rationale: Snapshots use VACUUM INTO so they are complete, compact and safe mid-sale; triggered every 20 transactions, every 30 minutes, on startup and shutdown, keeping the newest 30, and only when something actually changed.

nodes.label: Netlify Customer API (settings, products, orders, track)
Netlify Secrets Scan Guard (npm run check)
nodes.rationale: Only DB_PASS may be marked secret because Netlify searches for the exact value of every secret variable, and values like 4000 or pos-water-station appear in ordinary code and fail the build.

nodes.label: Owner Login (scrypt + session)
nodes.rationale: The owner password lives in the database (not the installer) so it can be changed from Settings -> Account and recovered with Reset Password.bat.
